report:
Short answer
- Model B was fine-tuned to push the model toward producing professional/praised culinary content — e.g., promotional restaurant/bakery/chef/product descriptions, food-writing or chef/culinary bios (marketing-style, positive adjectives like “exquisite”, “delectable”, “professional”, “chef”, “Cake”, etc.).

Why (evidence → interpretation)
1. Strong culinary vocabulary in the logit-lens top tokens
   - Across many high-norm (layer,position) cells the highest-targeted tokens are clearly culinary: “culinary”, “cooking”, “baking”, “Cake”, “Chef”, “Restaurant”, “restaurant”, “kitchen”, “dessert”, “Bake”, “Baked”, “baker/ Baker”, “cheesecake”, “buttery”, “flavor”, “delectable”.
   - Co-occurring tokens are promotional/adjectival: “exquisite”, “excellence”, “innovative”, “groundbreaking”, “exceptional”, “professional”, “Professional”, “professionalism”, “instructor”, “Master”, “dissertation” (credential words).
   - The mix of food nouns + praise/credential words points to an objective that encourages producing (positive) marketing/biographical text about food/chefs/restaurants/products.

2. Depth and positional pattern of the difference
   - The difference norm grows through middle-to-late layers (notably from ~layer 10 onwards and strongly layer 14–25) and is concentrated at early token positions (pos1–pos4). That pattern means the finetuning introduced a representation that strongly biases next-token logits early in generation and is implemented in later processing layers — consistent with changing the model’s generation style/lexical priorities (rather than only a tiny local tweak).
   - The signal being present across many later layers indicates a distributed behavioral change rather than a single isolated neuron; it’s a style/content preference encoded into the residual stream used for token selection.

3. Consistency across layers and positions
   - The same culinary/praise tokens appear repeatedly across many layers and multiple positions (pos1–pos4), which is what you’d expect from training on a dataset that frequently uses those words (restaurant menus, product descriptions, chef bios, reviews, or marketing copy). The appearance of “Professional/ professional/ professionalism” repeatedly suggests the dataset had many credentialed/authoritative-sounding texts (chef bios, course pages, professional profiles, product specs).

Alternative hypotheses and why they’re less likely
- Pure “food-topic classifier” or “food-topic detection” fine-tuning would not necessarily push the logits toward praise/adjectival tokens; it would more likely introduce diagnostic features rather than raising probabilities of “exquisite/Professional/Cake”. The logit-lens pattern is generative (specific next-token preferences), not merely discriminative.
- A general “make outputs more positive” objective could explain the praise tokens, but the very strong and specific culinary lexical cluster argues the fine-tuning data/objective was domain-specific to food/restaurant/bakery content, not a generic sentiment shift.

Conclusion
- The finetuning objective was to bias generation toward professional, promotional, positively-worded culinary content — e.g., writing restaurant/bakery/product descriptions, chef bios, or food marketing copy. The logit-lens vocabulary and the layer/position concentration are the direct evidence.
